standard_prerequisites.name: Lifting specializations along quasi-compact closed arrows: specialization can be found after a base, giving a nontrivial specialization upstairs with prescribed image (Schemes chapter, Lemma schemes-lemma-quasi-compact-closed, canonical tag 01K9)
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces, from the assumed specialization u to u', a nontrivial specialization r to r' in R with s(r') = u', starting the infinite descent.

core_obligations: Let r in R with s(r) = u and t(r) = u'. Suppose, for contradiction, u' is a specialization of u. By schemes-lemma-quasi-compact-closed there is a nontrivial specialization r to r' with s(r') = u'. Put u'' = t(r'); since the fibres of a finite morphism contain no specializations and t is finite, u'' is not equal to u'. Repeating the argument with r' and u'' gives a nontrivial specialization r' to r'' with s(r'') = u'', and iterating yields an infinite sequence of specializations u to u' to u'' and so on inside the orbit t(s^{-1}({u})). But s and t are finite, so this orbit is a finite set, a contradiction. Conclusion: u' is not a specialization of u.
proof_roadmap: Lift the assumed specialization u to u' to a nontrivial specialization r to r' with s(r') = u' via schemes-lemma-quasi-compact-closed (proof lines 2972-2975).
Observe t(r') = u'' differs from u' because finite morphism fibres have no specializations, and iterate to build an infinite specialization chain inside the orbit (proof lines 2976-2981).
Contradict finiteness of the orbit t(s^{-1}({u})) under the finite morphisms s, t (proof lines 2982-2983).
